AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A cooking pot
   B. A simple hand-washing device made from a container
   C. A type of soap
   D. A toothbrush

2. How should rubber gloves be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them dirty
   B. Wash with a stone
   C. Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   D. Throw them in a fire

3. What is poaching? (1 mark)
   A. Feeding wild animals
   B. Watering crops
   C. Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   D. Planting trees

4. Why is compost mixed into the planting hole? (1 mark)
   A. It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   B. It makes the hole shallow
   C. It kills the seedling
   D. It prevents growth

5. Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny? (1 mark)
   A. So the pipe becomes lighter
   B. So water drips slowly
   C. So the water is warm
   D. So water pours out fast

6. Which domestic animal is often kept in dry areas for milk and meat? (1 mark)
   A. Camel
   B. Pig
   C. Duck
   D. Rabbit

7. Which food group gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Water only
   B. Salt
   C. Energy-giving foods
   D. Protective foods only

8. What could a school use to make a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   B. A stone
   C. A wooden door
   D. A broom

9. Which of these root foods gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Kale
   B. Sweet potato
   C. Egg
   D. Milk

10. Why do we cook food? (1 mark)
   A. To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   B. To make it colder
   C. To make it dirty
   D. To make it disappear

11. What is soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Watering the garden
   B. Adding manure to soil
   C. The washing or blowing away of top soil
   D. Planting trees

12. Why do we use more than one method of scaring animals? (1 mark)
   A. It confuses farmers
   B. Animals can get used to one method
   C. It uses more soil
   D. One method is always cheaper

13. How long may carrot seeds take to sprout? (1 mark)
   A. One year
   B. One hour
   C. One to three weeks
   D. One day

14. Which of these is an improvised duster? (1 mark)
   A. A piece of clean old cloth
   B. A bottle
   C. A stone
   D. A tin

15. Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To colour them
   B. To make them raw again
   C. To cool them so they are easy to peel
   D. To make them larger

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain what a fruit is in plant growth. (2 marks)

17. Explain four ways germs can enter the body. (4 marks)

18. Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water. (2 marks)

19. Explain three mistakes to avoid when tacking. (3 marks)

20. What should be done with a paper dust mask that is dirty? (2 marks)

21. What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — A simple hand-washing device made from a container
   A tippy tap uses little water.

2. C — Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   Washing with gloves on avoids touching dirt.

3. C — Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   Poaching is against the law.

4. A — It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   Compost gives food and helps water retention.

5. B — So water drips slowly
   Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

6. A — Camel
   Camels survive in dry regions.

7. C — Energy-giving foods
   Carbohydrates and fats give energy.

8. A — A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   A bottle with small holes in its cap drips slowly.

9. B — Sweet potato
   Sweet potatoes are starchy.

10. A — To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   Heat kills germs and softens food.

11. C — The washing or blowing away of top soil
   Bare soil can be carried away by rain or wind.

12. B — Animals can get used to one method
   A mix of methods works better.

13. C — One to three weeks
   Carrot seeds are slow, so be patient.

14. A — A piece of clean old cloth
   Old cloth makes a duster.

15. C — To cool them so they are easy to peel
   Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Uneven stitches, pulling the thread too tight, using thread the same colour as the cloth, making a hard knot at the end (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is thrown away and replaced, not washed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for throwing, 1 mark for replacing.

21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.
